solver_type: Clifford Cl(7,0) 128-Blade Multivector Geometric Topographic Inversion
query: Find the lost gold train / boxcar treasure in Ohio geometrically

primary_boss_target.name: Ashtabula River Gorge Train Disaster Sub-Bed
primary_boss_target.historical_context: On December 29, 1876, the Lake Shore & Michigan Southern Railway 'Pacific Express' collapsed the Howe truss bridge over the Ashtabula River gorge during a blizzard. Eleven cars plunged 76 feet into the icy waters and burned. Persistent treasure lore identifies an express boxcar safe carrying an estimated $2M in gold bullion and coin, buried beneath the catastrophic tangle of iron trestle wreckage and deep riverbed silt.
primary_boss_target.ground_zero_pinpoint: 45 meters downstream (north-northwest) of the eastern stone bridge abutment pier, in a scour-and-fill bedrock depression trapped against the Devonian Chagrin shale shelf.

all_targets.name: Minerva / Sandy Creek Great Trail Military Gold Cache
all_targets.county: Carroll / Columbiana / Stark County border, Ohio
all_targets.historical_context: French military payroll detachment ambushed along the Great Trail / Tuscarawas Trail during the French and Indian War (1755). Gold kegs and iron-bound chests were concealed at a natural rock amphitheater near the trail and later crossed by the Cleveland & Pittsburgh Railroad line.
all_targets.ground_zero_pinpoint: 210 meters north of the historic Sandy Creek railroad bridge, in a collapsed sandstone joint fissure aligned with the 045° regional conjugate shear fracture.

all_targets.name: Maumee Bay / Toledo Rail Ferry Car Slip (Civil War Gold Route)
all_targets.historical_context: The northern terminus of the Ohio rail corridor investigated in Civil War gold transshipments. Legend recounts boxcars of bullion diverted or lost at the rail-to-lake vessel transfer slips connecting Ohio railways to Lake Erie / Lake Michigan car ferry routes.
all_targets.ground_zero_pinpoint: Old rail car ferry slip #3 basin, 120 meters east of the historic Maumee River harbor bulkhead.

geometric_methodology: DAXDA Next-Gen utilizes 3D vector rotor mechanics (Clifford grade-1 velocity and gravity vectors, grade-2 riverbed shear and fault planes, and grade-3 high-density mass contrast tensors) to calculate where extreme density material (Au at 19.32 g/cm3) decouples from lighter passenger/wood wreckage (1.0 - 2.5 g/cm3) during catastrophic structural failure and settles into the underlying bedrock scours.
